classification.difficultyReason: Construct a tree that stops immediately at black, update probabilities as cards are depleted, and identify three successive reds as the sole no-black path.

inlines.text: A bag contains three red cards and two black cards.
Mary takes a card from the bag at most three times. Every time she takes out a card, she does not replace it, and if she draws a black card she stops drawing any more cards.
Draw a probability tree to represent the possibilities of her card draws.

answer.short: $B$: black; $R$: red. Every branch ending in $B$ stops.
answer.worked: Let $B$ represent a black card and $R$ a red card. Label each branch with its probability, using the remaining cards after each draw. Stop each branch immediately after a black card; otherwise continue to the third draw.

spec.sourceRegion: Upper-right column, Chapter 8 Review Set One, question 4(a)
spec.description: Three-stage stopping probability tree, with stages progressing left to right and black branches above red branches.
spec.mathematics: First draw: B with 2/5 or R with 3/5. After R: B with 1/2 or R with 1/2. After RR: B with 2/3 or R with 1/3. Terminal paths are B, RB, RRB and RRR.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed tree appears only in answer editions.

inlines.text: What is the probability that she does not draw a black card?
Multiply the probabilities along the three-red-card path.

answer.worked:
She must draw three red cards without replacement.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{no black card})&=\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{2}{4}\times\frac{1}{3}\\P(\text{no black card})&=\frac{1}{10}\end{align*}$$
